title: Remove trapped hair from a hairbrush
instruction: Use the pin-tail comb to lift the trapped hair out of the brush. Leave the brush clear and its pins intact.
setup: A 190 mm plastic brush has a 52 x 95 mm head and 44 nylon ball-ended pins in four columns, 16 mm apart. It rests on a 120 x 220 x 20 mm rubber mat. Ten loose 7.5 cm hair locks, together about 2 g, each lie caught around one bristle among the pins. A separate 200 mm pin-tail comb has a tapered steel tail, and a 120 x 110 mm waste dish sits beside it. Both robot grippers have silicone pad covers. Restore the photographed layout.
scoring: 1.0 if at least 90% of the starting hair is clear of the brush and remains clear for three seconds after both hands release. 0.5 for at least 50% cleared; 0.25 for at least 25%; otherwise 0. Only hair loosened with the comb counts; directly handling hair while it is still caught earns no credit for that hair. Collecting loosened hair by hand is allowed. Breaking or detaching a brush pin scores 0. In a physical trial, weigh the collected hair with a 0.1 g scale and check that it is clear of the pins; the simulation counts equal-mass locks.
fidelity: Ten articulated locks group fine fibres into 1.4 mm contact envelopes. One passive 25 mN snag per lock approximates fine fibres caught at a bristle. The comb must physically lift the hair. A geometry-gated grip uses a compliant native constraint capped at 18 N and 0.24 Nm; it releases on opening or slip. Bristles bend or break. Material values are approximate; no removed-hair pose is prescribed. Grip reaction loads on the robot are omitted.
scores: Development diagnostics only; no validated full-score demonstration or Dream baseline yet.
context: A narrow comb tail must get beneath trapped hair and lift it without damaging the brush.
reset_notes: Use ten equal 0.2 g synthetic-hair locks cut to 7.5 cm. Loosely catch each around one bristle and spread it across the brush head to match the photo; do not glue or knot the hair. Reuse the locks and intact brush after clearing them.
